M.title: Cargo retry backoff uses 500ms base delay, 10-second maximum, with (retries-1)*3 second formula
M.facts: ["MAX_RETRY_DEFAULT = 3 (constant, line 82)","MAX_RETRY_SLEEP_S = 10 seconds (maximum delay between retries, line 83)","INITIAL_RETRY_SLEEP_BASE_MS = 500ms (minimum initial delay, line 87)","INITIAL_RETRY_JITTER_MS = 1000ms (random jitter added to initial delay, line 91)","Backoff formula for subsequent retries: ((retries - 1) * 3) * 1000 ms + 500ms base","Retry-After header from server (429/503 responses) can override calculated sleep, capped at MAX_RETRY_SLEEP_MS (line 129)","Configuration loaded via gctx.net_config()?.retry with fallback to MAX_RETRY_DEFAULT (line 102)"]
M.narrative: The retry mechanism uses a specific exponential backoff schedule: first retry waits 500-1500ms (base + jitter), second retry approximately 3.5 seconds, third retry approximately 6.5 seconds, with maximum 10-second cap. The server can override this via Retry-After headers on 429 and 503 responses. Default of 3 retries means maximum elapsed time approaches 20+ seconds under normal backoff, but server-controlled Retry-After can extend this further if needed for rate limiting scenarios.

The documentation describes the purpose as retrying "possibly spurious network errors" without detailing the exponential backoff timing or maximum sleep limits. The setting is also mentioned in context of slow HTTP connection detection which triggers retries based on transfer speed thresholds.

L.text: Investigated how cargo decides retry delay after HTTP 429, for the internal Artifactory crates.io mirror (60 req/min per IP, no Retry-After header on 429s). Logic lives in src/util/network/retry.rs. maybe_spurious() treats 429/5xx as retryable. Retry::try() calls parse_retry_after() first; it only returns Some() if a literal Retry-After header (seconds or HTTP-date) is present, else falls back to next_sleep_ms(): fixed exponential schedule ~0.5-1.5s, 3.5s, 6.5s, capped at MAX_RETRY_SLEEP_S=10s, for net.retry (default 3) retries = 4 total attempts. Also important: even when Retry-After IS present, the value is clamped to MAX_RETRY_SLEEP_MS (10s) via `.min(MAX_RETRY_SLEEP_MS)` at retry.rs:129 - cargo will never wait more than 10s per retry no matter what the server asks for.

L.text: Investigated where `cargo test` spawns test binaries after linking, for the Windows Defender file-lock issue (fresh .exe locked ~2s, spawn fails with 'Access is denied. (os error 5)'). Flow: src/ops/cargo_test.rs `run_tests` -> `compile_tests` (runs `ops::compile`, which links all test binaries) -> immediately `run_unit_tests`, which loops over `compilation.tests` and for each one builds a `ProcessBuilder` via `cmd_builds`/`compilation.target_process(...)` then calls `cmd.exec()` (crates/cargo-util/src/process_builder.rs:291). `exec()` -> `status()` -> `_status()` (line 263) builds a `std::process::Command` and calls `cmd.spawn()` directly (line 272) as a single, synchronous spawn attempt with no delay after linking finishes. The only existing retry path is `should_retry_with_argfile` (line 253), gated on `imp::command_line_too_big(err)` — that only matches argument-list-too-long errors (E2BIG-style), not access-denied. So a spawn failure from a transient AV file lock on a freshly linked binary has no retry/backoff anywhere in this path; it propagates immediately as a hard error via `ProcessError::could_not_execute`.

L.text: Infra team corrected the Artifactory crates.io mirror's rate limit from 60 req/min/IP to 120 req/min/IP. Checked the repo (src/util/network/retry.rs, tests/testsuite/publish.rs, src/util/progress.rs) for any hardcoded dependency on the 60 number — none exists. Cargo's retry logic doesn't rate-limit client-side against a request/min figure at all; it only reacts reactively to HTTP 429 + Retry-After (see obs #1: MAX_RETRY_SLEEP_MS caps at 10s regardless of server value), and net.retry default of 3 (obs #2 decision) is unrelated to the mirror's RPM cap. No code change needed; the 60 vs 120 figure was informational only, not encoded anywhere.
